name: Cubie
description:
About This Game

Change your perspective, change the rules

​Cubie is a minimalist 2D puzzle platformer where space isn't your enemy, but your greatest tool. Forget everything you know about traditional gravity—in this world, the physics depend entirely on how you enter a surface. Whether you approach from the left, right, top, or bottom, each side of the cube reorients your reality. What was an impassable abyss just a second ago can instantly become your new path forward.

The world of Cubie remains the same. Only your perspective of it changes.

Dynamic Gravity

Navigate all six sides of the cube. Every transition over an edge shifts the world’s orientation. Master the art of spatial thinking to find a way forward where others see only the edge of the map. In Cubie, your destination is often just one "flip" away.

Freedom in Rotation

​

​You are not just a victim of your environment. Take full control of your perspective. Survey the cube from every angle and decide which path to take. The ability to actively rotate the world allows you to pause, observe, and strategically outsmart each logical challenge. In Cubie, your next move is a matter of choice, not chance.

Interactive Mechanics

​

​Experience classic puzzle elements in an entirely new dimension. Push boxes, trigger floor switches, and unlock gates—but stay sharp. Every object is bound by the same laws of gravity as you. Always remember: a button on the ceiling is out of reach until you find the right perspective to make it your floor.

A Wealth of Challenges

  • Over 80 Unique Levels: From intuitive tutorials to complex logical labyrinths that will push your spatial imagination to its limits. Remember: there isn't always just one right way forward.

  • Minimalist Design: No unnecessary distractions. Just you, Cubie, and the pure satisfaction of a solved mystery. Focus on the logic, master the cube.
short_desc: CUBIE is a minimalist puzzle platformer where you control gravity. Each side of the cube offers unique physics based on how you enter it. The world remains the same – only your perspective changes. Can you solve spatial puzzles in a labyrinth where "up" is just a relative term?
